common.status.queued_checkpoint.notes: Status of a transcription stage that the power-aware policy put back in line (charger pulled, or moved to another device): it is waiting, but its checkpoint already holds this share of the lecture, and the next run continues from there instead of starting over. Shown in the stage card, the screen-reader label of the bar segment and the transcript page. Keep the word for checkpoint the same as common.pipe.k_checkpoint.

common.action.cancel.notes: Cancels a running or queued stage.

common.action.use_colab.notes: Button on the transcription stage's card (pipeline hover card) when Colab handed the lecture back and this computer has no transcription device that could take it (waiting.remote_fallback). Same action and wording as the lecture menu item menu.lecture.use_colab (“Process on Colab instead”, 改用 Colab 处理, SPEC-v3 V14.4): the transcription starts over on Google Colab after a confirmation. No period.

common.action.rerun_text_only.notes: Button on the transcription stage's card (pipeline hover card) and lecture context menu item, offered only when the transcript is worth repairing. “Fix sentence breaks” (修复断句, textrepair-int): for a lecture transcribed before LectureFlow learned to repair degenerate Whisper output, the transcript's long runs without punctuation and its all-caps passages are repaired by statistics learned from the same lecture's normal text (full stops added, capitals restored), and the sentences are split again. It does not transcribe the audio again. The same name is the confirm button (lecture.text_repair.ok). Short; no period.

common.class.auto.notes: Class of an AI repair: applied automatically.

common.class.absorb.notes: Class of an AI repair: minor, the translation absorbs it.

common.class.decide.notes: Class of an AI repair: the user should listen and decide.

common.review_state.pending.notes: Review state of an AI repair.

common.check.openvino_venv.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: whether .venv-ov exists (phase 3b).

common.check.openvino_devices.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: the Intel GPU / NPU / CPU that OpenVINO detected.

common.check.npu_driver.notes: Name of a diagnostics check: whether the NPU driver works.

common.check.mlx_python.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on macOS (mac-opti M3): the MLX transcription environment (asr-mlx component) is installed and its Python runs. The check named mlx (import) shows the product name MLX.

common.check.mlx_model.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on macOS (mac-opti M3): the files of the Apple GPU's Whisper model are there.

common.check.mlx_selftest.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on Apple silicon Macs (ext-step1): the MLX model transcribes one second of silence (run by “Check again”). Like common.check.cuda.

common.check.cpu_selftest.notes: Name of a diagnostics check on computers without an NVIDIA GPU or Apple silicon (ext-step1): one second of silence transcribed on the CPU (run by “Check again”).

common.check.colab_auth.notes: Name of a diagnostics check in the cloud group (ext-step1): a stored Google Colab credential.

common.check.colab_reach.notes: Name of a diagnostics check in the cloud group (ext-step1): Google Colab answers a free read-only request.

common.check.aria2c.notes: Name of a diagnostics row. aria2c is the download engine bundled with LectureFlow; it fetches lecture recordings for the browser extension and downloads app updates. {version} is the first line of `aria2c --version` (e.g. “aria2 version 1.37.0”), {sha256} a 64-character hex hash. Recording-related wording uses “fetch” (刮削), never “download”, by the user's decision.

common.check.browser_ext.notes: Name of a diagnostics row. The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), {browser} one name, {version} the extension's version, {at} a local time “YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM”. “Register again” (重新登记) is the button next to the row.

common.check.credentials.notes: Name of a diagnostics check (#/system): how the saved API keys and the Colab authorization are encrypted at rest (cred-enc).

common.check.data_dir_location.notes: Name of a diagnostics check (#/system), shown only with a warning: the data folder is in a cloud sync folder or on a FAT/exFAT drive.

common.pipe.k_speed.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card; the value is the real-time factor and how many times faster than real time the transcription ran.

params.speed: how many times faster than real time (1 ÷ rtf), e.g. '29'

common.pipe.rtf.notes: Keep the abbreviation RTF (real-time factor) as it is: it is the number shown in the device test results too.

common.pipe.k_load.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card; the value is how long loading the model took.

common.pipe.k_parts.notes: Row label in the transcription stage card: the run was resumed on another device (power-aware), one line per part.

params.combo: model and precision, e.g. large-v3-turbo · fp16 (not translated)

common.pipe.part.notes: One part of a resumed transcription in the stage card.

errors.check.browser_ext_unavailable.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), {browser} one name, {version} the extension's version, {at} a local time “YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM”. “Register again” (重新登记) is the button next to the row.

errors.check.browser_ext_in_use.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging); that program reaches the running LectureFlow through a private local connection (a named pipe on Windows, a socket on macOS). Changed (nm-harden, 2026-10-27): this LectureFlow could not open that local connection because another program already holds it (a second LectureFlow, or some other program that took the name first). The extension therefore cannot reach this LectureFlow. Do not suggest that the extension works through the other program: earlier versions of this text did, and it is not true. The hint (errors.check.hint_browser_ext_in_use) says what to do.

errors.check.hint_browser_ext_in_use.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging); that program reaches the running LectureFlow through a private local connection (a named pipe on Windows, a socket on macOS). Hint of errors.check.browser_ext_in_use (changed, nm-harden 2026-10-27): close whatever holds the connection (often another LectureFlow still running), then restart LectureFlow; if the message stays, restart the computer.

errors.check.hint_browser_ext_update.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), {browser} one name, {version} the extension's version, {at} a local time “YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM”. “Register again” (重新登记) is the button next to the row.

errors.check.browser_ext_blocked.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging). macOS only: the system refused LectureFlow access to the folder where the browser looks for such registrations, so the extension cannot connect through that browser. The hint (errors.check.hint_browser_ext_full_disk) says how to allow it. {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names (Chrome, Edge, Firefox).

errors.check.browser_ext_not_ready.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). The browser extension talks to LectureFlow through a small host program that is registered with Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Native Messaging). macOS only: the browser is installed but has never been started, so the folder where it looks for registrations does not exist yet (the browser creates it at its first start; LectureFlow must not). The hint says: open it once, then “Register again”. {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names; the verb may need to agree with one or several browsers.

errors.check.browser_ext_app_location.notes: Diagnostics page (系统诊断), row about the browser extension feature (SPEC-ext). macOS only: LectureFlow was opened straight from its downloaded disk image (.dmg), or macOS runs it from a temporary read-only copy (App Translocation, after it was opened from Downloads without moving it). When LectureFlow is closed, the browser extension normally starts it in the background; from such a place it cannot, because that place disappears. The hint (errors.check.hint_browser_ext_move_app) says to move it to Applications.

errors.check.hint_browser_ext_full_disk.notes: Hint of errors.check.browser_ext_blocked (Diagnostics page, browser extension row, macOS only). “System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access” is the path in Apple's System Settings app: use the names macOS itself shows in your language (zh-CN: 系统设置 › 隐私与安全性 › 完全磁盘访问权限; zh-TW: 系統設定 › 隱私權與安全性 › 完全取用磁碟). “Register again” (重新登记) must match the button's label (system.ext.register).

errors.check.hint_browser_ext_open_brows.notes: Hint of errors.check.browser_ext_not_ready (Diagnostics page, browser extension row, macOS only): start the named browser(s) once, then click the “Register again” button (重新登记; must match system.ext.register). {browsers} is a comma-separated list of browser names.

errors.check.hint_browser_ext_move_app.notes: Hint of errors.check.browser_ext_app_location (Diagnostics page, browser extension row, macOS only): drag LectureFlow into the Applications folder (use the folder's name as the macOS Finder shows it in your language; zh-CN: 应用程序), then open it from there.

errors.pdf.decode_budget.notes: Job error of extracting the text of a PDF: lecture slides (shown on the course page's slide row) or a PDF syllabus (shown in the syllabus wizard after uploading). Security review: the PDF's compressed contents unpack to far more data than any real slides or syllabus (a typical sign of a file built to exhaust the computer's memory), so LectureFlow stopped instead of continuing. Not retried automatically; a damaged or exotic export can also cause it, hence the advice to export the PDF again (e.g. from PowerPoint or the original program).

errors.pdf.memory_limit.notes: Job error of extracting the text of a PDF (lecture slides on the course page, or a PDF syllabus in the syllabus wizard). Security review: the text extraction process has a fixed memory limit so that a malicious or broken PDF cannot use up the computer's memory; this PDF needed more, so it was stopped. Not retried automatically. Same pattern as errors.pdf.decode_budget.

params.minutes: number of minutes (integer, at least 1; any value)

errors.pdf.timeout.notes: Job error of extracting the text of a PDF (lecture slides on the course page, or a PDF syllabus in the syllabus wizard). Security review: the extraction has a time limit that grows with the file size and the number of pages (real slides take a few seconds); this PDF took longer, so the process was stopped. Not retried automatically. Same pattern as errors.pdf.decode_budget; “min” as in errors.colab.queue_timeout.

params.name: file name inside the lecture's folder: “audio.wav” (the converted audio) or “stream.mp4” (the playback video); never a path

errors.prep.file_in_use.notes: Error of preprocessing (the lecture's first step, which converts the recording into audio.wav for transcription and stream.mp4 for the player) or of the playback-file step. Windows only: another program has that file open, so the newly made file could not replace it; the old file is unchanged. Most often it is this lecture playing in LectureFlow's own player (in a browser tab) or in an external player. LectureFlow tries again by itself a few times; after closing the player or program the user can select the stage's “Retry” button (common.action.retry). Use the same wording for that button as in common.action.retry.

The charger was unplugged: the transcription ran on a device that is not used on battery (e.g. the NVIDIA GPU); it is paused and continues on the same device when the power adapter is connected again.

errors.export.file_in_use.notes: Error of the export step (the lecture's last step, which writes the bilingual Markdown, the two subtitle files, the English text and the citation JSON), shown on the lecture page and in the pipeline card. Windows only: another program (an editor such as Word, a viewer, a download that is still running) has this export file open, so the new export could not replace it. Nothing was changed: all the old export files are still there and still downloadable. LectureFlow tries again by itself a few times; after closing the program the user can select the stage's “Retry” button (common.action.retry). Use the same wording for that button as in common.action.retry.

errors.media.no_h264_encoder.notes: Error of the playback-file step (SPEC-v3 V7): the video needs converting but no H.264 encoder can be used, so the player opens in audio mode. Shown on the lecture page and in the player.

errors.media.encoder_failed.notes: Error of the playback-file step (SPEC-v3 V7, qsv-retry): the video had to be converted to H.264 and the video encoder itself failed (e.g. the graphics chip's hardware encoder glitched under load), also after a second try and with every other usable encoder. The file is fine and trying again may work, so the player opens in audio mode meanwhile. Shown on the lecture page and in the player after “Could not create the playback file:” (player.audio.failed). params.tried (encoder names) is not shown.

params.format: an untranslated technical name: the kind of playlist found (m3u8, ffconcat, pls, xml, mpd, smil, asx, xspf, sdp) or ffmpeg's name of the detected container or protocol (hls, concat, nut, caf, http); “?” when unknown

errors.media.format_rejected.notes: Error of preprocessing (the lecture's prep step) or of the playback-file step, shown on the lecture page, in the pipeline card and in the player after “Could not create the playback file:”. The lecture's stored media file turned out to be a playlist or a container outside the accepted list. Security review 2 (M3): ffmpeg follows playlists (HLS .m3u8, ffconcat scripts), which could make it read other files on the computer or connect to a network share with the user's Windows credentials, so LectureFlow refuses them. New uploads are already checked (errors.upload.media_format); this covers media stored earlier or added another way. A started lecture's media cannot be replaced, so the remedy is converting the file and uploading it again. Same meaning as errors.upload.media_format, without the file name.

errors.upload.media_format.notes: Upload of a lecture recording or a second camera view (also a finished browser-extension fetch): ffprobe detected a container format outside the accepted list. Security review 2 (M3): ffmpeg follows playlists (HLS .m3u8, ffconcat scripts), which could make it read other files on the computer or connect to a network share with the user's Windows credentials, so LectureFlow refuses them. The remedy is converting the file to a common format (MP4, MKV, MP3). No period at the end.

errors.data_import.network_path.notes: Settings → data folder → import the data folder of the development version (desktop app). The imported database stores paths to lecture recordings or slides on another computer (UNC paths such as \\server\share\…), outside the folder being imported. Opening such a path makes Windows connect to that computer and send the user's sign-in credentials, so the import is refused. The last sentence: when the whole data folder lives on a network share, choosing it by the same path (e.g. the \\server\share\… path rather than a mapped drive letter) makes its paths count as inside it. Ends with a period like the other errors.data_import.*.

errors.downloads.needs_refresh.notes: HTTP 409 of POST /api/downloads/{id}/retry for a fetch that needs a refresh: only the extension can bring new cookies. Second sentence = downloads.needs_refresh.hint.

errors.downloads.credentials_cleared.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>) or as a toast for an HTTP error. No period at the end (like the other errors.*). New (queue2). A fetch failed; LectureFlow kept the sign-in data (cookies) in memory so that 重试/Retry works without the recording page, but only for {minutes} minutes. Nobody retried in time, so the data was deleted for safety and the task is now in state needs_refresh. The second sentence matches errors.downloads.needs_refresh.

errors.downloads.drm_protected.notes: A fetch task of the browser extension (录播刮削任务) stopped: the stream is DRM-protected. Wording chosen by the user (neutral statement, never mention circumventing). Complete sentences with a period.

errors.downloads.angle_no_video.notes: A fetch task of the browser extension stopped: the second picture of the “dual camera” option has no video. “Main audio and video” must match the popup's option label (主要音视频).

errors.downloads.tls_failed.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>) or as a toast for an HTTP error. No period at the end (like the other errors.*). State failed (retryable). aria2c or LectureFlow refused the HTTPS certificate of the recording's server (e.g. “Invalid certificate chain”): usually a man-in-the-middle by a school/company proxy or an antivirus “HTTPS scanning” feature, which LectureFlow does not trust. The advice: another network, or turn that inspection off.

params.host: the refused host name or IP address, e.g. 10.0.0.5 or media.campus.example.edu

errors.downloads.local_address.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>). No period at the end (like the other errors.*). State failed; retrying does not help. A URL of the recording (an entry of its playlist, a redirect, or an address its host name resolves to) is on the user's local network (a private or link-local address, a *.local name) while the page the recording was sent from is on the public internet: LectureFlow refuses so that a web page cannot make it send requests inside the user's own network (security review). Recordings whose page is itself inside the network (a school's server reached over VPN) are not refused. “Local network” = the LAN at home or at school, not the internet.

params.host: the refused host name or IP address, e.g. 127.0.0.1 or localhost

errors.downloads.loopback_address.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): shown under a fetch task row on the course page (Download.error, errors.<code>). No period at the end (like the other errors.*). State failed; retrying does not help. A URL of the recording leads to this computer itself (127.0.0.1, localhost, or a name that resolves to it): never fetched, whatever the page (security review: a web page must not make LectureFlow send requests to programs running on the user's computer).

params.host: the refused host, when a task was refused while running (not shown)

errors.downloads.site_blocked.notes: Fetch queue of the browser extension (SPEC-ext; recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载), see glossary §9): LectureFlow refused a page or a track on a site it does not handle — YouTube, or an online course platform (MOOCs, paid courses such as Udemy or Coursera; user decision 2026-10-27). Shown by the extension when a send is refused, and under a fetch task row on the course page if a playlist or redirect led to such a site. Wording by the lead (plain, not preachy); the extension's errSiteBlocked is the same sentence. Complete sentence with a period.

errors.selfupdate.not_newer.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”): LectureFlow checks GitHub Releases (or mirrors the user added) for a signed update.json, downloads the installer and installs it at the next start; “Update from file” (从文件更新) takes update.json, update.json.minisig and the installer for offline use. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. No period at the end (like the other errors.*). update.json and update.json.minisig are file names: keep them as they are. Offline update with an older or equal version (downgrade protection). Versions look like 3.2.0.

errors.selfupdate.import_incomplete.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”): LectureFlow checks GitHub Releases (or mirrors the user added) for a signed update.json, downloads the installer and installs it at the next start; “Update from file” (从文件更新) takes update.json, update.json.minisig and the installer for offline use. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. No period at the end (like the other errors.*). update.json and update.json.minisig are file names: keep them as they are. params.missing (manifest, signature, package) is a code and not shown.

errors.selfupdate.import_invalid.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”): LectureFlow checks GitHub Releases (or mirrors the user added) for a signed update.json, downloads the installer and installs it at the next start; “Update from file” (从文件更新) takes update.json, update.json.minisig and the installer for offline use. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. No period at the end (like the other errors.*). update.json and update.json.minisig are file names: keep them as they are. params.file is the user's file name.

errors.selfupdate.sources_invalid.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”): LectureFlow checks GitHub Releases (or mirrors the user added) for a signed update.json, downloads the installer and installs it at the next start; “Update from file” (从文件更新) takes update.json, update.json.minisig and the installer for offline use. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. No period at the end (like the other errors.*). update.json and update.json.minisig are file names: keep them as they are. Settings: the list of extra update sources (mirrors). params.index is the 0-based row and not shown. Security review: sources must be https; plain http only for an address of this computer (127.0.0.1, localhost).

params.path: absolute path of the data folder (not shown)
params.who: account names as Windows or macOS reports them, comma-separated (e.g. “Authenticated Users, Users”); keep as they are

errors.selfupdate.untrusted_dir.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”), security review: the data folder lets other accounts of this computer change files (typical when it was moved to a drive such as D:\, where every signed-in account may modify new folders). LectureFlow then neither downloads nor installs updates from it, because another account could swap the files. Shown on the settings page's update section or as a toast. “Diagnostics” (诊断) is the page #/system, where the data folder row offers “Restrict access”. No period at the end (like the other errors.*).

errors.selfupdate.no_manifest.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates, under the line settings.update.state.no_manifest: a check reached GitHub (or a mirror), but the latest release has no update.json or no update.json.minisig yet (HTTP 404). This is what users see between the moment a new version is published and the moment the maintainer uploads its signature, usually a few hours. Say clearly that it is not the user's network (the older text for unreachable sources asked them to check it). LectureFlow checks again by itself after about 2 hours when automatic checks are on; the next line says when. update.json is a file name: keep it. No period at the end (like the other errors.*).

waiting.on_battery.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: battery awareness keeps the NVIDIA card idle on battery (waiting_for on_battery).

waiting.memory.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: an Intel device needs more system memory than is free (waiting_for memory).

waiting.no_asr_device.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: no device is turned on and detected (waiting_for no_asr_device). 'Transcription' is the settings section name (settings.block.asr).

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost"), not translated

waiting.device_selftest.notes: What a transcription stage waits for: its device runs a device test (waiting_for device_selftest:{id}).

waiting.power_wait_ac.notes: What a transcription stage waits for (waiting_for power_wait_ac): on battery, a transcription of a device that is not used on battery (e.g. the NVIDIA GPU) continues on that device when the power adapter is connected. Keep the "<status>: power-aware - <reason>" structure of the source. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

waiting.power_no_saver_device.notes: waiting_for power_no_saver_device: on battery neither an NPU nor an Intel GPU is turned on and detected (the NVIDIA GPU and the CPU are never used on battery). Also the resource monitor's note when no device is active. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

waiting.power_no_device.notes: waiting_for power_no_device: a laptop plugged in has no NVIDIA GPU or Intel GPU turned on and detected (or none of the devices chosen by hand); a laptop never transcribes on the CPU. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)

waiting.power_queue.notes: waiting_for power_queue:{id}: the one active device of a laptop is busy; the task is not given to another device. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.from: the device running now (name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated))
params.to: the device chosen for the new power state

waiting.power_switch_pending.notes: waiting_for power_switch_pending:{from}:{to}: e.g. the charger was plugged in while the NPU runs a lecture; plugging in never interrupts a transcription, the next one starts on the new device. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)

waiting.power_device_selftest.notes: waiting_for device_selftest:{id} on a laptop (one active device at a time): the active device runs a device test, the task waits for it instead of going to another device. On a desktop waiting.device_selftest is shown. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

waiting.remote_queue.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_window.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_auth.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_balance.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it is sent to Google Colab (SPEC-v3 V14.5). Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon may join two parts.

waiting.remote_busy.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when only Google Colab can take it and Colab is busy with another lecture (Colab transcribes one lecture at a time) or is still starting or shutting down; it starts by itself when Colab is free. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period.

waiting.remote_fallback.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) after Google Colab handed the lecture back (notes.remote.back_to_local is shown next to it) while this computer has no transcription device that could take it: it would wait for good. The stage card offers the button common.action.use_colab (= menu.lecture.use_colab, “Process on Colab instead”); the second part points to it without quoting it exactly. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon joins the two parts.

waiting.remote_held.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) after the user pressed one of the Colab shutdown buttons (resources.remote.after_current “Shut down after this lecture” / resources.remote.now “Shut down now”): sending lectures to Colab automatically stays paused while lectures wait (resources.remote.held), and this computer has no transcription device that could take the lecture, so it would wait until the user acts. The stage card offers the button common.action.use_colab (= menu.lecture.use_colab, “Process on Colab instead”), which also ends the pause; the second part points to it without quoting it exactly. “As you asked” = the pause is the user's own choice, not a fault. Same style as waiting.remote_fallback: phrase, no period; a semicolon joins the two parts. zh-CN addresses the user as 你, like the rest of the interface.

waiting.no_provider.notes: What a stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) in the “Transcription only” setup (3.1.0; onboarding.tier.transcribe_only.*): correction, translation and the summary need a model service and wait until one is set up in Settings, then continue by themselves. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period. “Model service” = what onboarding calls a service (an API provider).

waiting.remote_offline.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it may run only on the user's own SSH inference servers (Settings → Remote servers; ssh-mvp) and the server cannot be reached now: LectureFlow is connecting or reconnecting; it starts by itself when the server is back. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period.

waiting.remote_setup.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) when it may run only on the user's own SSH inference servers (Settings → Remote servers; ssh-mvp) and the server is reachable but its transcription environment (Python packages and the Whisper model) is not installed yet or is being installed. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period.

waiting.remote_fallback_ssh.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) after one of the user's own SSH inference servers handed the lecture back (it is never sent to a remote device automatically again) while this computer has no transcription device that could take it. The Colab counterpart is waiting.remote_fallback. Same style as the other waiting.* keys: phrase, no period; a semicolon joins the two parts.

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070", "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics"), not translated

waiting.component_missing.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for component_missing:{id}): this computer has the device, but the software it needs to transcribe (a component such as “NVIDIA GPU transcription”, installed under Settings → Components, the settings section settings.comp.title) is not installed yet, typically right after a fresh install. The lecture waits and starts on its own once the component is installed; nothing to retry. Same style as waiting.device_paused / waiting.memory: phrase, no period; the colon (zh) or semicolon (en) joins what is missing and what to do. zh-CN addresses the user as 你 (here implicit), like the rest of the interface.

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070", "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics"), not translated

waiting.model_missing.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for model_missing:{id}): the device's transcription software is installed, but the Whisper model chosen for that device (its model setting in the transcription device settings, settings.block.asr) is not installed as a component. Two ways out: install that model under Settings → Components, or switch the device to a model that is installed (its model setting under Transcription in the settings). The lecture then starts on its own. Same style as waiting.component_missing: phrase, no period.

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070", "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics"), not translated

waiting.component_installing.notes: What a transcription stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for component_installing:{id}): the component the device needs (its transcription software or its model) is being downloaded or installed right now (also while that download is paused); the lecture starts on the device once it is done. Neutral, no urgency. Phrase, no period, like waiting.device_slot.

waiting.retry_backoff_due.notes: What a stage is waiting for (job.waiting_for) once the countdown of waiting.retry_backoff ('Retrying automatically in {n} seconds') has reached zero: the automatic retry starts within a second, or as soon as a slot is free. Also the {wait} of common.summary.failed_wait ('{stage} failed. {wait}').

player.angle.name_1.notes: Player (ext web3): a lecture with a second camera view (e.g. sent by the browser extension as "Two cameras", or added on the lecture page) shows the other view as a small picture in a corner of the video (picture in picture). Clicking the small picture swaps the two views; the sound always comes from the main view. Name of the lecture's own video (with the sound); shown as the label on the small picture after a swap and in the swap button text.

lecture.text_repair.message.notes: First paragraph of that dialog: why it is offered (long passages without punctuation or in capitals) and what it does. “Fix sentence breaks” (修复断句, textrepair-int): for a lecture transcribed before LectureFlow learned to repair degenerate Whisper output, the transcript's long runs without punctuation and its all-caps passages are repaired by statistics learned from the same lecture's normal text (full stops added, capitals restored), and the sentences are split again. It does not transcribe the audio again. The four points below it are lecture.text_repair.no_transcribe, keep_reviewed, downstream and patches.

lecture.text_repair.no_transcribe.notes: Point 1 of the dialog (a list item, a complete sentence): the audio is not transcribed again; only the stored text changes; it is quick (seconds).

lecture.text_repair.keep_reviewed.notes: Point 2: sentences the user reviewed and edited by hand (human_text) are kept exactly as they are. Address the user directly (你 / you).

lecture.text_repair.downstream.notes: Point 3: the stages after transcription (summary, AI correction = 修复, the LLM correction stage common.stage.repair, translation and export) become out of date and run again automatically, which costs LLM usage of about 0.2 yuan (CNY, ¥) per lecture; keep the amount and the currency.

lecture.text_repair.patches.notes: Point 4: the review's records of accepting or rejecting the AI correction's suggestions (patches) are cleared; the review starts again from the new suggestions.

lecture.text_repair.ok.notes: Confirm button of that dialog; the same words as common.action.rerun_text_only.

resources.title.notes: Title of the resource monitor (right column)

resources.gpu.paused.notes: Label next to the switch (narrow column)

resources.devices.pause_all_title.notes: Title of the dialog asked before pausing every device while transcriptions run (its message is nav.gpu.pause_message).

params.device: the device's own name (e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost"), not translated

resources.devices.device_switch.notes: Switch on one device card: pauses or resumes that device only.

resources.devices.idle.notes: A device card without running tasks.

resources.devices.battery_mode.notes: Tag on a device card while the computer runs on battery (SPEC-v2 I10).

resources.devices.battery_mode_tip.notes: Hover text of the tag "Battery · power-aware" on the active device card and of the power line while a laptop runs on battery: the battery rules of the power-aware policy. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.devices.util_na.notes: Hover text of “--” in the usage tile of an Intel device.

resources.devices.temp_na.notes: Hover text of “--” in the temperature tile of an Intel device card (no Windows counter reports it without administrator rights).

resources.devices.apple_mem.notes: Row label on the Apple GPU's card in the resource bar (mac-opti M6): how much of the unified memory the GPU holds, shown against the installed memory (e.g. 1.6 GB / 16 GB).

resources.system.title.notes: Upper section of the resource monitor: CPU, memory, CPU temperature and the power state the power-aware policy follows.

resources.system.cpu.notes: Tile label (narrow, half of the monitor's width): total CPU usage in percent.

resources.system.mem.notes: Row label: physical memory used / installed (e.g. 14.2 GB / 31.7 GB). Also used as the label of an Intel device's shared GPU memory on its card (used / available, e.g. 2.9 GB / 15.8 GB).

resources.system.cpu_temp.notes: Tile label (narrow): the highest thermal zone temperature; "--" when the computer reports none.

resources.system.unified_mem.notes: Resource bar, upper area, on Apple silicon (mac-opti M6): replaces resources.system.mem; the memory used / installed is the unified memory the CPU and GPU share (Activity Monitor's “Memory Used”).

resources.system.stream_bg_one.notes: Resource panel, system area: one lecture's playback file (browser-playable video) is being converted in the background, in parallel with transcription.

resources.system.stream_bg_many.notes: Resource panel, system area: several lectures' playback files are being converted in the background at the same time. n is always 2 or more.

resources.system.stream_bg_tip.notes: Hover text of the background playback-file line in the resource panel: why it runs separately and that it does not use a transcription device (GPU/NPU slot), only one CPU slot.

resources.power.ac.notes: Power source in the resource monitor: external power (power adapter or USB-C; they cannot be told apart reliably).

resources.power.battery.notes: Power source in the resource monitor: running on battery.

resources.power.level.notes: Battery charge next to the power source.

resources.power.charging.notes: Tag next to the power source: the battery is charging.

resources.power.not_charging.notes: Tag next to the power source while plugged in: the battery is not charging (e.g. full).

resources.power.no_battery.notes: Tag next to the power source of a desktop: no battery, so the power-aware rules do not apply.

resources.power.basis_tip.notes: Hover text of the power row: this is the state the power-aware device choice follows.

resources.power.wait_ac.notes: Line in the power section: transcriptions suspended on battery until the power adapter is connected. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.power.wait_no_device.notes: Line in the power section: transcriptions suspended because no device qualifies under the power-aware rules. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.active.title.notes: Middle section of the resource monitor: the device(s) the power-aware policy uses now (cards), with the main pause switch.

resources.power.reason.ac_auto.notes: Tag on the active device card: why this device — plugged in, chosen automatically (NVIDIA GPU, else Intel GPU).

resources.power.reason.battery.notes: Tag on the active device card: why this device — on battery, the power-aware choice (NPU, else Intel GPU).

resources.power.reason.manual.notes: Tag on the active device card: the device is in the list chosen in Settings (Transcription device: choose devices yourself).

resources.power.reason.desktop.notes: Tag on the device cards of a computer where no battery is detected — a desktop, or a laptop whose power state cannot be read: the device list's order, several devices at once. Must not say "desktop": a laptop with an unknown power state gets it too.

resources.power.reason.switch_pending.notes: Tag on the active device card instead of the reason tag when the charger was plugged in (or the preferred device changed) while this device runs a lecture: it finishes the lecture, then the preferred device takes over (hover: resources.power.next). Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

params.device: name of a transcription device, e.g. "Intel(R) AI Boost" (the device's own name, not translated)

resources.power.next.notes: Note on the active card after the charger was plugged in (or unplugged): the running lecture finishes here, the next one starts on {device}. Power-aware policy (laptops, power management): must be recognisable as the deliberate power-aware policy, not a fault; keep the word for "power-aware".

resources.power.manual_ignored.notes: Note in the middle section: devices are chosen in Settings, but on battery the power-aware choice applies.

resources.standby.title.notes: Bottom section of the resource monitor: the devices not in use now, one row each; a row opens its details.

resources.standby.standby.notes: Tag of a device row: turned on, not used now (the power-aware policy uses another device).

resources.standby.untested.notes: Small tag of a device row: the device test has never run on it.

resources.standby.holds_suspended.notes: Tag of a device row: a transcription suspended by the power-aware policy continues on this device when plugged in.

resources.rail.asr_power.notes: Collapsed monitor, while the power-aware policy suspends transcriptions.

resources.balance_failed.notes: Used when the reason has no translation of its own

params.when: relative time, such as “3 minutes ago”

resources.col.cache_hit.notes: Column header: cache hit rate (narrow column)

resources.missing_holidays.notes: Note in a provider row of the resource monitor

settings.provider.endpoint_openai.notes: Hint under the type in the add / edit provider dialog; follows the base_url field as the user types (3.2.0: it showed the literal text {base_url}, which read as a placeholder left unfilled)

params.base_url: the base_url field's value as typed (e.g. https://api.anthropic.com, trailing slashes removed), or https://… while the field is empty; shown in code style together with the path written right after it, so keep the path directly after {base_url}

settings.provider.rpm_range_hint.notes: Hint under the “Requests per minute” field of the provider dialog: the allowed range; 0 switches the per-minute limit off.

params.limits: the current limits as on the diagnostics page: system.api.limits (e.g. “8 concurrent · 300/min”) or system.api.limits_unlimited
params.max: the recommended number of requests at a time, 64

settings.provider.limits_old.notes: Info banner inside a provider row of Settings → Providers, only for a provider of DeepSeek’s official API whose limits are still the old conservative defaults of earlier versions (8 at a time / 300 per minute or lower). Explains why translation is slow, that DeepSeek limits concurrent requests per account only, and what the recommended limits are. The button settings.provider.limits_apply follows. Nothing is changed unless the user clicks it.

settings.provider.limits_apply.notes: Small button of the banner settings.provider.limits_old: sets the provider to the recommended DeepSeek limits the banner names (64 at a time, no per-minute limit).

settings.provider.limits_applying.notes: The button settings.provider.limits_apply while the change is being saved.

settings.provider.limits_applied.notes: Toast after the recommended limits were saved for the provider.

settings.provider.key_moved_hint.notes: Warning hint under the API key field of the provider dialog (editing an existing provider that has a key), shown while base_url points to a different host, scheme or port than before and the key field is empty. For security the server removes the stored key when the provider moves to another host, so the user has to type the key again (sec2-app L2).

settings.provider.key_unreadable_chip.notes: Chip next to a provider name on the settings page when its saved API key cannot be decrypted (the data folder came from another computer or Windows/macOS account). Like settings.provider.no_key_chip.

settings.provider.key_unreadable.notes: Value of the API key fact of such a provider (instead of the masked key).

settings.provider.key_unprotected_chip.notes: Chip next to a provider name when its API key is stored in the clear: it was saved while LectureFlow had no encryption key (Windows DPAPI or the macOS Keychain failed). Sealed at the next start that has a key.

settings.asr.redecode.notes: Settings page, section 转写 (Transcription): form row label of a switch, on by default (user request 2026-10-27). On: when Whisper writes a 30-second decoding window as one long run without punctuation or all in capital letters, LectureFlow transcribes that window again with the preceding text as a prompt and keeps the new version only if it passes checks. “退化” = degenerate: the window's text lost its normal punctuation and capitalisation. Short; no period.

settings.asr.redecode_hint.notes: Hint of the row settings.asr.redecode. Keep all points: (1) on by default; (2) what triggers it: a 30-second window without punctuation or in all capitals; (3) what it does: that window is transcribed again with the text before it, and the new result replaces the old one only if it is better; (4) the cost: affected lectures take about 30–70% longer to transcribe, depending on the lecture (keep the numbers); (5) off: only the statistical repair runs (统计修复 = a text-only repair of capitalisation and sentence boundaries, no second transcription); (6) it applies to later transcriptions and does not make existing lectures need a rerun. Complete sentences.

settings.colab.memory_label.notes: Settings page, section “Colab remote transcription”, group “How to use” (settings.colab.use_title): the switch of Colab's memory mode, on by default (user's decision of 2026-10-27). On: the recording, the faster-whisper model and the Python packages stay on a RAM disk of the Colab runtime instead of its persistent disk; a lecture that does not fit uses the disk. Short; no period. Terms: 运行时 = runtime (the Colab machine, glossary §9); “Python 软件包” = Python packages, as in settings.comp.sources_hint.

settings.colab.memory_hint.notes: Hint under the switch settings.colab.memory_label. Keep all four points: (1) it is on by default; (2) the recording, the model and the Python packages stay in the runtime's memory and are not left on its disk; (3) when there is not enough memory, that lecture automatically uses the disk; (4) the boundary from SPEC-ext: the runtime is still Google's machine, so this does not make the data invisible to Google — never promise that Google cannot see it. Complete sentence(s). Terms: 运行时 = runtime (the Colab machine, glossary §9); “Python 软件包” = Python packages, as in settings.comp.sources_hint.

settings.colab.accel_default.notes: 已废弃，不需要翻译或修改（DEPRECATED: no longer used by the settings page since colab-obs (replaced by settings.colab.accel_default_account); do not translate or change). Earlier note: Settings page, section “Colab remote transcription”, under the accelerator select (settings.colab.accel_label), shown only while the user has never picked an accelerator: then the tier decides (user decision 2026-10-27: paid tier = L4, free tier = T4). Once the user picks one, it is never replaced. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Complete sentence.

settings.colab.accel_info_title.notes: 已废弃，不需要翻译或修改（DEPRECATED: no longer used by the settings page since colab-obs (the accelerator radio list has no heading); do not translate or change). Earlier note: Heading of a small list under the accelerator select: what each Colab GPU measured on a real 55-minute lecture with the large-v3 model — the time the lecture takes on Colab and the compute units it costs (colab-prof, 2026-10-27). The list items are settings.colab.accel_info.* after the GPU's name. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. No period.

settings.colab.accel_info.T4.notes: One item of the list under settings.colab.accel_info_title, after the GPU name “T4”. Measured: about 3.8 minutes and about 0.07 compute units for a 55-minute lecture; a T4 transcribes one lecture at a time. Keep the numbers. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Fragment, no period.

settings.colab.accel_info.L4.notes: One item of the list under settings.colab.accel_info_title, after the GPU name “L4”. Measured: about 3 minutes and about 0.08 compute units for a 55-minute lecture; it can transcribe two lectures at once, and in a batch (two at once) each lecture costs about 0.05 compute units — the cheapest per lecture. Keep the numbers. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Fragment, no period.

settings.colab.accel_info.A100.notes: One item of the list under settings.colab.accel_info_title, after the GPU name “A100”. Measured: about 2.3 minutes and about 0.2 compute units for a 55-minute lecture; two lectures at once. Keep the numbers. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Fragment, no period.

settings.colab.accel_info.G4.notes: One item of the list under settings.colab.accel_info_title, after the GPU name “G4”. Measured: about 1.9 minutes and about 0.28 compute units for a 55-minute lecture; two lectures at once. Keep the numbers. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Fragment, no period.

settings.colab.fast_label.notes: Settings page, section “Colab remote transcription”: the switch of “fast mode” (user decision 2026-10-27: an option, off by default). On the larger GPUs (L4, A100, G4) each lecture is cut at silent moments into parts that are transcribed at the same time. Short; no period. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture.

settings.colab.fast_hint.notes: Hint under the switch settings.colab.fast_label. Keep every point: off by default; only the L4, A100 and G4 GPUs (no effect on a T4); a lecture is cut at silences into 2–4 parts transcribed at once; 15–60% less time (about 1 minute for a 55-minute lecture on a G4); the result differs slightly from transcribing the whole lecture — about 3–4% of the words, and more differences in capitals, punctuation and where sentences break (be honest: never say it is the same); while on, these GPUs transcribe one lecture at a time instead of two at once. Terms: 计算单元 = compute units (glossary §9); 显卡 = GPU; 讲座 = lecture. Complete sentences.

params.accelerator: the GPU currently selected, e.g. T4 (a code, not translated)

settings.downloads.title.notes: Settings: title of the section (and its entry in the section list) for fetching the recordings the browser extension sends. Recordings are “fetched” (刮削), never “downloaded” (下载): see glossary §9.

settings.downloads.intro.notes: Settings → Fetching: the line under the title. aria2c is the fetch tool's name: keep it.

settings.downloads.concurrency_label.notes: Settings → Fetching: how many lectures are fetched at the same time (1–6, a row of numbers). Wording: 同时刮削数 (user decision 2026-10-27: recordings are fetched, not downloaded; the spec said 同时下载数).

settings.downloads.connections_label.notes: Settings → Fetching: how many connections one file uses while fetching (1–16, a drop-down). Wording: 单任务连接数 (2026-10-27; the spec said 单任务线程数, but the value is a number of connections).

settings.downloads.connections_cap.notes: Settings → Fetching: grey text next to the connections drop-down: the platform's profile may set a lower limit (maxConnectionsPerFile), and the smaller one is used. Wording given by the lead.

settings.downloads.load_error.notes: Settings → Fetching: the section could not be loaded (with a retry button). Same pattern as settings.app.load_error.

settings.update.label.notes: In-app update (SPEC-ext “应用内更新”): LectureFlow checks GitHub Releases (or mirrors the user added) for a signed update.json, the user downloads the installer, and it is installed at the next start. Settings > App: title of the row with the update status, after “Update channel”.

settings.update.hint.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the small hint under the row title. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.privacy.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: privacy note with a shield icon under the status. “Mirrors” is the row settings.update.sources_label. Complete sentence with a period.

settings.update.state.idle.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: status line before any check since the start (a “Check now” button follows). Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.checking.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: status line while a check runs (spinner). Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.up_to_date.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last check found nothing newer. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.available.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: a newer version was found; a “Download” button and a line with the release date, installer size and “Release notes” follow. A “Beta” tag may follow for a beta release. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.downloading.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: download in progress, with a progress bar and “Cancel download”. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.importing.notes: In-app update, Settings > App: shown while the files of “Update from file” are checked (signature, version, size, SHA-256). Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.pending.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the new version is downloaded (or imported from files) and verified; the desktop app installs it the next time it starts. A “Discard” button follows. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.check_failed.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last check failed; the reason (errors.selfupdate.*) follows on the next line. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.download_failed.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last download failed; “Download again” follows and the reason (errors.selfupdate.*) is on the next line. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.state.no_manifest.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the status line instead of “Checking for updates failed” (settings.update.state.check_failed) when the latest release has no update.json or signature yet (errors.selfupdate.no_manifest follows on the next line). Calm wording: nothing is broken on the user's side. Status phrase, no period.

settings.update.not_configured.no_public.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: this build has no update key, so it cannot update itself (the only row of the section). “Releases page” is the GitHub Releases page, as in errors.selfupdate.*. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.not_configured.dev_build.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: a development build (its version is not a release version). Complete sentence with a period.

settings.update.not_configured.unsupport.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the operating system or processor has no release package (3.x: Windows x64 and Apple silicon Macs only). Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.not_configured.no_source.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the updater could not start (no place for its files and settings; should not happen in a normal installation). Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.not_configured.web_mode.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates in web mode (the server run without the desktop app), next to the “Desktop app only” tag. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.no_source.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: why a check failed when no update source is known (no GitHub repository built in and no mirror added). Shown in place of errors.selfupdate.not_configured, so like the errors.* texts no period at the end. “Update from file” is the title of the row below (settings.update.file_label); quote it exactly.

settings.update.check.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: check for a new version now.

settings.update.download.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: download the new version (nothing downloads before this click).

settings.update.retry_download.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: after a failed download.

settings.update.cancel_download.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: stops the download; the part already downloaded is kept for the next attempt.

settings.update.download_note.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: small line under the download progress, explains “Cancel download”. Complete sentence with a period.

params.total: size of the installer, e.g. 180.4 MB

settings.update.progress.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: under the progress bar.

params.when: relative time or date from the code, e.g. “3 hours ago”, “today 09:12”, “2 Nov”

settings.update.released.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: release date of the new version, in a line “Released … · Installer: … · Release notes”.

settings.update.size.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the size of the installer (the package of this installation), in a line “Released … · Installer: … · Release notes”.

settings.update.notes.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: link to the release page with the release notes (opens the browser).

params.when: relative time or date from the code, e.g. “3 hours ago”, “yesterday 14:20”

settings.update.last_check.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: when the last check ran (by hand or automatically).

settings.update.discard.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: drop the update that waits for the next start (asks first, settings.update.discard_title).

settings.update.discard_title.notes: In-app update: title of the confirmation dialog of “Discard”. A question.

settings.update.discard_message.notes: In-app update: text of the confirmation dialog of “Discard”. “Update from file” is the row title settings.update.file_label; quote it exactly. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.discard_ok.notes: In-app update: the confirming (danger) button of the “Discard” dialog.

settings.update.origin_file.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: under the pending update when it came from “Update from file” (not downloaded). Phrase, no period.

params.previous: the running version that is kept, e.g. 3.1.0

settings.update.rollback_to.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: under the pending update. Complete sentence with a period.

params.when: relative time or date from the code, e.g. “today 08:00”

settings.update.result.installed.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: the last installation succeeded (shown while that version runs). Phrase, no period.

params.from: the version LectureFlow went back to, e.g. 3.1.0

settings.update.result.rolled_back.notes: In-app update: the new version did not start and the desktop app restored the previous one. Shown in Settings > App > App updates (with “Details”: the reason in English) and for a week as a warning line at the bottom of the Dashboard. Complete sentences with a period.

params.version: the version that could not be installed

settings.update.result.failed.notes: In-app update: the installation failed before anything was replaced. Shown in Settings > App > App updates (with “Details”) and for a week at the bottom of the Dashboard. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.details.notes: In-app update, Settings > App: disclosure that opens the technical reason (English, from the updater or the desktop app) under an error or a failed installation. Same wording as the other “查看详情”.

settings.update.file_label.notes: In-app update, Settings > App: title of the row for offline updates (desktop app). The errors.selfupdate.* texts and settings.update.no_source refer to it as “Update from file”: keep them identical.

settings.update.file_hint.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > Update from file: hint under the row title. update.json and update.json.minisig are file names: keep them as they are. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.file_drop.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > Update from file: text of the drop area, next to the “Choose files” button (common.choose_files).

settings.update.file_done.notes: In-app update: toast after “Update from file” accepted the files. Short, no period (like the other toasts).

settings.update.auto_label.notes: In-app update, Settings > App: title of the row with the on/off switch for automatic checks.

settings.update.auto_hint.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > Check automatically: hint. Since 3.2.0 a failed check is retried sooner (after 1, 3 or 6 hours; every 2 hours while the latest release has no update information yet), a successful one waits a day. “Download” and “Check now” are the buttons settings.update.download and settings.update.check; quote them exactly. Complete sentences with a period.

settings.update.sources_label.notes: In-app update, Settings > App: title of the row with the extra update sources (mirrors or proxies of GitHub). errors.selfupdate.unreachable and download_failed tell the user to “add a mirror in Settings”: same word.

settings.update.sources_max.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > Mirrors: shown instead of the formats note when the list is full. Complete sentence with a period.

settings.update.last_check_failed.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: a note under a new version that can still be downloaded or installed (“Version 3.2.1 is available”, “… will be installed the next time LectureFlow starts”) when the most recent check failed. The version found before stays offered; only the latest check did not succeed. No period at the end (the error text ends the sentence).

settings.update.next_check.notes: In-app update, Settings > App > App updates: after a failed check, when LectureFlow checks again by itself (it retries after 1, 3 or 6 hours, every 2 hours while the release has no update information yet, otherwise once a day). settings.update.version_unbound.notes: In-app update: replaces errors.selfupdate.version_mismatch when the signature's trusted comment names no version at all (signed with minisign's default comment instead of LectureFlow's “lectureflow update version:…”). The update is refused because the signature cannot be tied to the version. “Trusted comment” is minisign's term (a signed comment line in update.json.minisig); keep it recognizable. Shown in Settings > App > App updates (check or Update from file). No period at the end (like errors.*).

This line says that this copy of LectureFlow also lets the developer build of the extension connect (the one loaded from the source code, “Load unpacked”), because LectureFlow itself is a development build (built from source, without a release version). Use the same name for the “developer build” of the extension as docs/install.md and the extension pages do.

system.ext.dev_extension_env.notes: Diagnostics page, row "Browser extension connection" (check browser_ext), a line under the browsers' registration. Like system.ext.dev_extension_build, but the reason is that the user (a contributor) set the environment variable LECTUREFLOW_DEV_EXTENSION=1 for an installed LectureFlow. downloads.list_label.notes: Accessible name of the list of recording fetches above a course's lecture table (recordings the LectureFlow browser extension sent).

downloads.untitled.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Shown instead of the title when the recording platform gave none.

downloads.state.queued.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag (chip) of a fetch waiting for a free slot. Same word as the stage state 排队中 (glossary).

downloads.state.downloading.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag of a running fetch; followed by the progress (downloads.progress).

downloads.state.merging.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag: the fetched pieces (HLS segments, or the audio and the video track) are being joined into one media file.

downloads.state.importing.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag: the finished file is turned into a lecture draft (a few seconds), then transcription starts.

downloads.state.done.notes: State tag of a finished fetch (its lecture exists). The course page does not show finished fetches; kept for other views.

downloads.state.failed.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag of a failed fetch; the reason is on the row's second line, with a Retry button.

downloads.state.needs_refresh.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag: the recording site's sign-in (cookies) is no longer there or no longer accepted (e.g. after the app restarted, or it waited too long). The user resumes it by opening the recording page again and clicking the extension (downloads.needs_refresh.hint). Wording from the spec: 需要刷新.

downloads.state.cancelled.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). State tag of a fetch the user cancelled (its files are deleted).

params.n: place in the fetch queue, 1 = next

downloads.position.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). After the tag 排队中 / Queued: where the fetch is in the queue of all courses.

downloads.progress.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). After the tag 刮削中 / Fetching (and 需要刷新: what is kept for resuming).

downloads.progress_unknown.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Progress while the size is not known yet (a playlist whose segments are still being counted).

downloads.track.audio.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). A track of the fetch that has no name from the platform's profile; tracks are listed after the title, e.g. “音频、视频”.

downloads.track.video.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). See downloads.track.audio.

downloads.needs_refresh.hint.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Second line of a fetch that needs a refresh (downloads.state.needs_refresh): what the user does to continue it; what was fetched is kept. Wording given by the spec (SPEC-ext, ext-brief §6.2). “LectureFlow” is the product name: keep it. No period. errors.downloads.restarted, credentials_rejected, credentials_expired, needs_refresh and credentials_cleared end with exactly this text (the page checks whether the reason already contains it): keep the six identical.

params.reason: why it needs a refresh, an errors.downloads.* sentence (e.g. the app restarted)

downloads.reason.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). After downloads.needs_refresh.hint, in grey.

downloads.failed_unknown.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Second line of a failed fetch when the server sent no reason (normally an errors.downloads.* sentence is shown).

downloads.details.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Disclosure under a failed fetch's reason: opens the fetch tool's own message (aria2c or ffmpeg, in English). Same wording as the other “查看详情” the error texts point to (e.g. errors.downloads.merge_failed).

downloads.action.retry.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Button of a failed fetch: queue it again.

downloads.action.cancel.notes: Course page: one row per recording fetch above the lecture table (in the look of the upload rows). Button of a fetch that has not ended: stop it and delete what was fetched. Also the confirm button of downloads.cancel_confirm.*

downloads.cancel_confirm.title.notes: Title of the question before cancelling a fetch that has already fetched something.

downloads.cancel_confirm.message.notes: Body of the question downloads.cancel_confirm.title. Buttons: downloads.action.cancel (danger) and downloads.cancel_confirm.keep.

downloads.cancel_confirm.keep.notes: The cancel button of the question downloads.cancel_confirm.title: closes it and the fetch goes on.

params.n: recordings queued, fetching, merging or creating their lecture (plural forms)

downloads.dash.active.notes: Workbench (dashboard): a line under the title while recordings sent by the browser extension are fetched, parts joined with “ · ”, e.g. “正在刮削 2 节录播 · 1 节需要刷新”, then links to the courses.

params.n: recordings whose fetch needs a refresh (plural forms)

downloads.dash.needs_refresh.notes: Workbench line (downloads.dash.active), in the warning colour: fetches waiting for the user to open the recording page again (downloads.state.needs_refresh).
